concept.name: Responsive selling
concept.definition: In Market Profile/auction terminology, responsive selling is selling that appears above the established value area — the 'expected' behavior of sellers responding to prices that are expensive relative to accepted value. Responsive selling caps rallies at value area highs and rotates balanced markets back toward the point of control.
concept.intuition: Responsive sellers are profit-takers at rich prices: when the market trades above agreed value, they sell into the strength.
concept.mechanics: Identified by selling activity at/above the prior VAH accompanied by rotational (non-trending) structure; its presence supports mean-reversion reads, while its absence at the highs warns that initiative buying may be in control.
concept.failure_modes: Fading strength on the assumption of responsive selling fails on trend days, when the expected sellers at the highs never arrive; the classification is only as good as the value area it is measured against.
concept.misconceptions: Selling above value is not inherently a top signal — it is the routine behavior that maintains balance, and it becomes dangerous exactly when balance is breaking.
concept.example: A rally stalls at yesterday's VAH of 4,540 as sell programs repeatedly offer the level; price rotates back to the POC — responsive selling performing its range-maintaining role.

citations.source: FuturesIndicators — Trading With Market Profile: Practical Setups (responsive selling above the value area)
